note.en: Namuchi is named in the Vishnu Purana among the Danava sons of Viprachitti by Sinhika, alongside Vatapi and Ilwala.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book I, Chapter XXI ("The sons of Viprachitti by Sinhika (the sister of Hiranyakasipu) were Vyansa, Salya the strong, Nabha the powerful, Vatapi, Namuchi, Ilwala, Khasrima, Anjaka, Naraka, and Kalanabha...")

verification.notes: Wilson's Vishnu Purana Book I Chapter XXI lists Namuchi among the sons borne to Viprachitti by Sinhika.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book I, Chapter XXI ("The sons of Viprachitti by Sinhika (the sister of Hiranyakasipu) were Vyansa, Salya the strong, Nabha the powerful, Vatapi, Namuchi, Ilwala, Khasrima, Anjaka, Naraka, and Kalanabha...")

verification.notes: The same Vishnu Purana Book I Chapter XXI list names Vatapi immediately before Namuchi among the sons of Sinhika.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book I, Chapter XXI ("The sons of Viprachitti by Sinhika (the sister of Hiranyakasipu) were Vyansa, Salya the strong, Nabha the powerful, Vatapi, Namuchi, Ilwala, Khasrima, Anjaka, Naraka, and Kalanabha...")

verification.notes: The same Vishnu Purana Book I Chapter XXI list names Ilwala immediately after Namuchi among the sons of Sinhika.

note.en: Brihaspati rouses the hiding Indra by recalling his slaying of Namuchi along with Samvara and Vala.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Udyoga Parva, SECTION XVI ("O Indra, the great Asura Namuchi was killed by thee; and those two Asuras also of terrible strength, viz., Samvara and Vala")

verification.notes: Ganguli's Mahabharata, Udyoga Parva SECTION XVI, has Vrihaspati remind Indra that he slew the great Asura Namuchi.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, SECTION LXV ("Namuchi and Pauloman; Asiloman, and Kesi and Durjaya; Ayahsiras, Aswasiras, and the powerful Aswasanku")

verification.notes: Adi Parva SECTION LXV enumerates Namuchi in its catalogue of the Danavas born of Danu.

note.en: The Vishnu Purana names Sinhika as the sister of Hiranyakasipu and the mother of Danavas by Viprachitti.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book I, Chapter XXI ("The sons of Viprachitti by Sinhika (the sister of Hiranyakasipu) were Vyansa, Salya the strong, Nabha the powerful, Vatapi, Namuchi, Ilwala, Khasrima, Anjaka, Naraka, and Kalanabha...")

verification.notes: Vishnu Purana Book I Chapter XXI parenthetically identifies Sinhika as the sister of Hiranyakasipu.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book I, Chapter XIX, note ("Rahu was the son of Sinhika, more known as the dragon head, or ascending node, being a chief agent in eclipses")

verification.notes: Wilson's note to Vishnu Purana Book I Chapter XIX states that Rahu was the son of Sinhika.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book I, Chapter XXI ("The sons of Viprachitti by Sinhika (the sister of Hiranyakasipu) were Vyansa, Salya the strong, Nabha the powerful, Vatapi, Namuchi, Ilwala, Khasrima, Anjaka, Naraka, and Kalanabha...")

verification.notes: Vishnu Purana Book I Chapter XXI lists Vatapi among the sons of Viprachitti by Sinhika.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book I, Chapter XXI ("The sons of Viprachitti by Sinhika (the sister of Hiranyakasipu) were Vyansa, Salya the strong, Nabha the powerful, Vatapi, Namuchi, Ilwala, Khasrima, Anjaka, Naraka, and Kalanabha...")

verification.notes: Vishnu Purana Book I Chapter XXI lists Ilwala among the sons of Viprachitti by Sinhika.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book I, Chapter IX, note ("In the Padma and Bhagavata, Rahu and Ketu are the sons of Sinhika, the wife of the Danava Viprachitti")

verification.notes: Wilson's note to Vishnu Purana Book I Chapter IX records the Padma and Bhagavata making Rahu and Ketu the sons of Sinhika, wife of Viprachitti.

note.en: The Mahabharata's roll of divine consorts sets Rudrani beside Rudra as Lakshmi is beside Narayana.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Udyoga Parva, SECTION CXVII ("as Surya with Prabhavati, Agni with Swaha, Vasava with Sachi, Chandra with Rohini, Yama with Urmila, Varuna with Gauri, Kuvera with Riddhi, Narayana with Lakshmi, Sagara with Jahnavi, Rudra with Rudrani")

verification.notes: Ganguli's Mahabharata, Udyoga Parva SECTION CXVII, pairs Rudra with Rudrani in its list of divine couples.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Sabha Parva, SECTION XI ("Rudrani, Sree, Lakshmi, Bhadra, Shashthi, the Earth, Ganga, Hri, Swaha, Kriti, the goddess Sura, Sachi Pushti, Arundhati... these and many other goddesses wait upon the Creator of all")

verification.notes: Sabha Parva SECTION XI names Rudrani first among the goddesses who wait upon the Creator in the court of Brahma.

note.en: The Vishnu Purana names the eleven Rudras as Hara, Bahurupa, Tryambaka, Aparajita, Vrishakapi, Sambhu, Kaparddi, Raivata, Mrigavyadha, Sarva, and Kapali.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book I, Chapter XV ("There are eleven well-known Rudras, lords of the three worlds, or Hara, Bahurupa, Tryambaka, Aparajita, Vrishakapi, Sambhu, Kaparddi, Raivata, Mrigavyadha, Sarva, and Kapali")

verification.notes: Vishnu Purana Book I Chapter XV places the account of the eleven Rudras immediately before the daughters of Daksha given to Kasyapa.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book I, Chapter XV ("There are eleven well-known Rudras, lords of the three worlds, or Hara, Bahurupa, Tryambaka, Aparajita, Vrishakapi, Sambhu, Kaparddi, Raivata, Mrigavyadha, Sarva, and Kapali")

verification.notes: Vishnu Purana Book I Chapter XV enumerates the eleven well-known Rudras by name and calls them lords of the three worlds.

note.en: Sarama, the celestial bitch, curses the sacrifice of Janamejaya after his brothers beat her son without cause.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, SECTION III ("there arrived at the spot an offspring of Sarama (the celestial bitch)... And she addressed Janamejaya in anger")

verification.notes: Adi Parva SECTION III opens with the whelp of Sarama beaten at the sacrifice of Janamejaya and Sarama upbraiding the king.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Sabha Parva, SECTION XI ("Aditi, Diti, Danu, Surasa, Vinata, Ira, Kalika, Suravi, Devi, Sarama, Gautami and the goddesses Pradha, and Kadru;--these mothers of the celestials")

verification.notes: Sabha Parva SECTION XI counts Sarama among the mothers of the celestials attending the court of Brahma.

note.en: Shashthi appears in the Sabha Parva among the goddesses who wait upon Brahma in his assembly hall.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Sabha Parva, SECTION XI ("Rudrani, Sree, Lakshmi, Bhadra, Shashthi, the Earth, Ganga, Hri, Swaha, Kriti, the goddess Sura, Sachi Pushti, Arundhati... these and many other goddesses wait upon the Creator of all")

verification.notes: Sabha Parva SECTION XI names Shashthi among the goddesses in attendance upon Brahma.

note.en: Wilson records the Padma Purana tradition that Vach bore the Apsarasas and the Gandharvas.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book I, Chapter XXI, note 21 ("The Padma, second series, makes Vach the mother of both Apsarasas and Gandharbas")

verification.notes: Wilson's note 21 to Vishnu Purana Book I Chapter XXI reports the Padma Purana making Vach the mother of both Apsarasas and Gandharvas.

note.en: Pashupati, lord of creatures, is the name the Mahabharata uses for Shiva, glossed as such in the Adi Parva.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, SECTION CXLVI ("the sacrifice which Pasupati (Siva) hath commenced in the town of Varanavata")

verification.notes: Ganguli's Mahabharata, Adi Parva SECTION CXLVI, glosses the name directly as Pasupati (Siva).

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Bhishma Parva, SECTION VI ("There the illustrious Pasupati himself, the creator of all things, surrounded by his celestial attendants and accompanied by Uma, sporteth")

verification.notes: Bhishma Parva SECTION VI describes Pasupati sporting on the Karnikara hills accompanied by Uma.

note.en: The account of the planetary spheres in the Vishnu Purana gives Sani a chariot drawn by piebald steeds and the slowest course of the grahas.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book II, Chapter XII ("the tardy-paced Sani (Saturn) moves slowly along in a car drawn by piebald steeds")

verification.notes: Vishnu Purana Book II Chapter XII describes the slow-moving car of Sani among the planetary chariots.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book II, Chapter VIII ("the sun was in Visakha, the moon in Krittika, Venus in Pushya, Jupiter in Purvaphalguni, Mars in Ashadha, Budha in Dhanishtha, Sani in Revati, Ketu in Aslesha, and Rahu in Bharani")

verification.notes: Vishnu Purana Book II Chapter VIII lists Sani in Revati alongside Ketu and Rahu in a single planetary configuration.
